backing.backing_score_basis: MEASURES THE SURPLUS BUFFER, NOT BACKING-OVER-SUPPLY — and for this asset those two carry OPPOSITE SIGNS. ⚠️ The feed's collateral ratio is `100 + (vow surplus buffer / supply)`, which the feed itself documents; it is NOT backing/supply. Gross backing minus supply is +$17.6M while the published `surplus_deficit` is −$66.4M. Both are correct and they answer different questions, so a reader who re-divides backing by supply will reproduce a quotient without reproducing the basis. ⚠️ Every USDS is minted 1:1 against a debt position, so par coverage is ~100% BY CONSTRUCTION and carries no information — the buffer is the entire signal. INHERITED from usds 7.0 and re-verified, not independently derived: sUSDS holds no reserve of its own, its collateral IS USDS's reserve, so a wrapper cannot outrank the asset it wraps on that asset's own book. Re-measured 2026-09-06: USDS+DAI backing $11.22B against $11.21B supply. Held at 7.0 because the buffer improved from the −$74.4M at last scoring and holders are unimpaired at par.

backing.backing_score_denominator: ⚠️ ASK WHAT THE RATIO DIVIDES BY BEFORE QUOTING IT. The feed's ~99.41% is surplus-based, not backing-based. Recovering the real denominator: D' = backing − surplus.

liquidity.liquidity_score_basis: ⚠️ MEASURES POCKET BALANCE — INVENTORY ON A FIXED-RATE ROUTE — NOT SLIPPAGE, BECAUSE A DEPTH LADDER MEASURES NOTHING FOR THIS ASSET. Re-grounded 2026-09-07 after the ladder was found NOT SIZE-RESPONSIVE: every rung from $1,000 to $1,000,000 returns an identical 0.00bps, and $5M, $10M, $25M, $50M and $100M all return a constant 1078.15bps — identical to the hundredth of a basis point across a 20x range. ⚠️ THAT IS A REDEMPTION RATE BEING RETURNED AS A QUOTE, NOT A FILL. A ladder that returns the same answer at every size bounds nothing, so the 8.5 was re-derived from inventory on the exit route rather than from executable depth. ⚠️ THE OLD BASIS IS RETRACTED BY NAME: the 8.5 previously rested partly on 'deep permissionless DEX liquidity, ~$7.5M/24h', and that claim is not measurable for this asset. ✅ CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE FEED, which reached the same conclusion by its own route: `two_pct_depth_status: not_size_responsive` and `total_2pct_depth_is_floor: true`. The $1,000,000 the dashboard shows is A FLOOR, NOT A MEASUREMENT — do not read it as depth that was tested and cleared.
liquidity.liquidity_score_persistence: filtered — exit-route structure and inventory, not spot depth
liquidity.liquidity_score_depth_caveat: ⚠️ ANY DEPTH BAND RENDERED BESIDE THIS SCORE IS MEASURING A QUANTITY THAT DOES NOT EXIST FOR sUSDS. The ladder is constant across a 20x size range; a 2% crossing figure here is a floor flag, not a cleared rung. Comparing this 8.5 against a computed depth band is comparing two different questions.

dependencies.underlying_score_basis: MEASURES CONCENTRATION OF THE COUNTERPARTY SET, NOT ITS QUALITY — which is why it sits LEVEL with Backing rather than below it. The dependencies are high quality; what this axis records is that they are concentrated rather than diverse. (1) 100% of this asset's value passes through ONE other asset: every risk in usds is a risk here, and no diversification is possible at this layer. (2) ⚠️ ~35% of USDS backing is USDC, so sUSDS is CORRELATED TO USDC, NOT DIVERSIFIED FROM IT — `usdc_raw_pct` 35.41%, range-bound 32.89–40.17% across the window. The March 2023 precedent is the point: DAI followed USDC down through the same module. Read sUSDS as roughly two-thirds diversified collateral plus one-third USDC. (3) A less-transparent credit sleeve at ~14.8% (OTC crypto lending 9.64%, AAA corporate 4.99%, private credit 0.21%) — high-grade on paper, materially harder to look through than a T-bill, and ⚠️ DRIFTING THE WRONG WAY: crypto lending 29.18% -> 30.66% of the sleeve while T-bills fell 15.78% -> 13.85%. ⚠️ BACKFILLED FROM THE PUBLISHED SURFACE, WHICH IS THE UNUSUAL DIRECTION: tidresearch had carried a fully-argued 7.0 while the internal source of record had no axis 4 at all. Load-bearing figures were re-measured before adoption, not copied — one passed, one drifted.
